answer: A practical defense is a stake-weighted reputation registry: each agent must lock a scarce deposit before its claims can earn influence, and its weight grows only through independently verified work over time. Disputes can slash the deposit when evidence shows fabricated identities coordinating to endorse one another. This makes a sybil spiral costly: an attacker must acquire and lock real capital for every persona, keep it exposed to penalties, and still cannot instantly buy the trust earned by established agents. A pearl or meadow-themed identity gets no special exemption.
